subject: Validate every `iovec` base address instead of special-casing null
notes:
make format changed nothing; make check exited 0 with no rustfmt, clippy, typo or license-header findings (log at /tmp/check-qMdgxS.log; the sole warning is rustup's benign implicit-toolchain-override notice). Both run from the worktree with the osdk prefix.

DEVIATION FROM fix.json, worth the parent agent's attention: the fix phase listed a third changed file, test/initramfs/src/regression/io/file_io/iovec_err.c, where it added a 65-line `bad_iov_base` case. It is NOT in this commit. phases/fix.md is explicit that a repro is scratch, 'never committed, and never added to test/initramfs/src/regression/', and phases/commit.md directs staging the kernel change and the pool edit specifically and confirming 'no repro file survives in test/initramfs/src/regression/'. So the file was reverted with `git checkout --` before staging and the regression directory is byte-identical to base e8f2b9ca6. The hunk is preserved verbatim at patch.diff:107-182 and can be applied as its own change if wanted -- note it was the only guard on the write direction (writev/pwritev/sendmsg), which fix.json flags as having no conformance coverage at all, so that half of the fix now ships unguarded in-tree. The kernel diff and the pool edit are unaffected; iovec_err.c was a pre-existing tracked file that the fix extended rather than created, which is why the call was a judgement rather than a mechanical cleanup.

Staged the two paths by name, not `git add -A`. The staged diff is 49 insertions / 12 deletions, and the pool edit removes exactly the three lines in select.json's pool_entries, leaving the other three and the file's missing trailing newline untouched. After committing, `git status --untracked-files=all` shows only .osdk/.crates.toml, .osdk/.crates2.json and .osdk/bin/cargo-osdk -- the harness's per-run OSDK install recorded as osdk_bin in state.json, build infrastructure rather than a source artifact, deliberately left out. The tracked tree is clean. One commit on top of base e8f2b9ca6, parent confirmed. Not pushed, no PR, nothing amended.

Message style follows the log: imperative subject at 66 chars naming the kernel change with identifiers in backticks, not the test name. The body gives the root cause (one predicate, `len == 0 || base == 0`, doing both the emptiness test and, accidentally, the validation gate, with its two clauses producing the two different wrong answers), states diagnose.json's invariant including the corollary that a null base is not itself invalid, and names the owning layer -- the iovec import layer at copy_iovs_and_convert, the only point that sees the whole vector before any transfer -- with the reason it owns the rule (all-or-nothing across the vector, six shared callers, so a fix in preadv.rs would leave pwritev and the sockets defective) and the two rejected alternatives (preadv.rs, and ostd's VmSpace which already checks correctly and was merely never reached). Linux's `__import_iovec` is cited as the reason both halves of the expected behavior are right -- access_ok not gated on length, and never rejecting NULL -- not as the justification on its own. It also records the two load-bearing design choices: reusing VmSpace's own MAX_USERSPACE_VADDR predicate so the eager and lazy checks cannot disagree, and the separate length pass that keeps EINVAL ahead of EFAULT, the divergence round 2 of the fix caught. Since gvisor_filter is set, the last paragraph names the three enabled cases and says the binary's other three stay blocked, distinguishing the two that still fail from ReadvTest.NotReadable_Pipe, which is stale-green but a different root cause and left to its own change.
